We started this project because hostel food logging is a pain, honestly most of us gave up after a few days. Our first try with a simple classifier failed because a thali has many dishes, so we switched to YOLO after our guide suggested it. We clicked about 700 photos ourselves in the canteen and labelled them by hand, which took ages. The first accuracy was bad, around 40 percent, mainly because dal and sambar look the same.

In today's rapidly evolving technological landscape, such systems play a pivotal role in empowering users to make informed dietary decisions. By leveraging state-of-the-art deep learning methodologies, the proposed solution seamlessly bridges the gap between computer vision and nutritional science. Furthermore, it fosters sustainable healthy habits and paves the way for innovative, personalised health interventions. In conclusion, this project stands as a testament to the transformative potential of artificial intelligence in addressing real-world challenges and delivering valuable insights to a wide range of stakeholders.
